text: Homework: A study of Flags and FTR's The purpose of this homework study is to identify flags before or after price breaks a key level, and identify what happens on the return to those flags. Does price react on the FTB / 2ndTB ext. Does price break straight through and then form an FTR ext. I will also add other pieces of the puzzle if I see them but the main focus for now is on flags.

Dr Swing's journal Post 291

It got me thinking, Firstly I thought this looks like a FO! Then I thought QM level & FO?

Then I thought I've just posted a chart with similar characteristics, an engulf of a flag down, creating an FTR and a great reaction when price returned to the FTR.

Question is a QM level often the return and reaction of price to a previously created FO?

Conclusion I think a study of QM's and FO's is required.

author: Aaron
text:
Beautiful mate!

I am very big fan of QMs now, I was not to begin with, but once you study why the ITs do it, it makes total sense in confusing unaware retailers tempting BO traders to go long on the HHs if we're in supply of course, and then stopping retailers out on the reverse, then once again tempting retailers to go short on the LL in the form of a BO, causing total confusion,

As you probably already know some of the QMs work to the PIP, others have a little DD, but all in all it is a GREAT way to look at the market
